classification_definitions.METHOD-SEMANTIC_ASSUMPTION: A fixed-N restriction in the tested scientific method; any such restriction would block E5-v2.
classification_definitions.EXPERIMENT-INFRASTRUCTURE_ASSUMPTION: A launcher, default list, readiness, logging, or campaign-specific fixed-N choice that may be parameterized without changing scientific semantics.
classification_definitions.NONE-N-AGNOSTIC: No fixed-N assumption; ordinary computations may legitimately depend on input cardinality.

components.reason: U is a unique integer array with no maximum length; cardinality checks depend on formation semantics, not N=8. Mission compilation iterates all nodes/tasks.

The production node default ALL_UAV_IDS ends at 10, but the uav_ids ROS parameter accepts any non-empty unique list and the Candidate parser consumes that dynamic availability. E5-v2 must pass registered IDs explicitly. uint8 IDs admit 1..16. No production edit is needed.
States are keyed by arbitrary integer ID; all-or-nothing freshness/skew checks iterate the requested participant set.
The centroid divides summed participant positions by len(U); no fixed cardinality/topology occurs.
Line, Circle, Polygon, and Sphere generate exactly count offsets. Triangle's exactly-three restriction is shape semantics, not an eight-agent assumption.
r_nominal and r_safe use the generated geometry's delta_min, so legitimate N-dependent scales arise without changing multipliers, safety floors, or workspace bounds.

Nx3 arrays, Hungarian assignment, pair combinations, group-local swap ranges, and trajectory sampling derive size from inputs. The optional exhaustive fallback is bounded by candidate count for computational reasons and is not required for acceptance.
Assignments are permutations of range(len(U)); one command/profile is generated per resolved participant.
Final duration is derived from the maximum assigned displacement and profiles are zipped across U/start/target. Analytic per-UAV limits are unchanged.

Each controller iterates a configured vector of neighbor IDs and accumulates all fresh neighbor interactions; no eight-neighbor topology is encoded. uint8 IDs and uint16 diagnostic counts cover N<=16.

Default launch/config ID lists end at 10, but swarm_launch parses the supplied uav_ids, creates one namespaced node per ID, and overrides neighbor_uav_ids with that full list. E5-v2 must pass the registered list; no controller source/config edit is required.
Namespaces /px4_i, target system i+1, ports, spawn offsets, and -n instance creation are arithmetic in ID/N. The external launcher supports up to 255 instances. E5-v2 supplies -n 8/12/16.
Nodes execute in graph order, snapshots use each task's U, and completion trackers iterate the resolved participants.
Disjoint groups are flattened dynamically, d_plan aggregation remains the frozen maximum rule, assignment stays group-local, and synchronized completion uses dynamically resolved tasks.
Offending pairs, per-UAV dynamics, J_hard, d_min, active/stale neighbor counts, failsafe, and readiness are emitted per dynamic ID set.

The historical CLI default is IDs 1..8 and its directory name is system_8uav, but the gate and subscriptions already iterate --uav-ids. E5-v2 provides an experiment-local dynamic-ID readiness/smoke wrapper.
These closed calibration/legacy harnesses contain explicit eight-UAV lists. They are not production method code and will remain immutable; E5-v2 uses new experiment-local infrastructure.
The old registry intentionally freezes availability [1..8]. It remains byte-immutable and is not reused or generalized.
